canonicalMutations.rationale: A clip is reusable musical content, independent of any position on a timeline.

payload.name: Clip
payload.statement: A clip owns reusable notes and timing. Editing a clip changes the musical content shared by its placements; it does not give the clip a timeline position or a placement-specific transpose value.

canonicalMutations.rationale: A placement gives one use of a clip its own timeline and playback settings.

payload.name: Placement
payload.statement: A placement references a clip and owns its timeline position and transpose value. Several placements can reference the same clip while retaining different positions and transpose values.

canonicalMutations.rationale: Musicians need to reuse one phrase at different pitches without copying and diverging its source notes.

payload.title: Transpose each placement independently
payload.statement: Each placement MUST store its own transpose value in semitones. Playback MUST apply that value to the referenced clip's notes without changing the clip. Two placements of one clip MAY have different transpose values. Saving and reloading an arrangement MUST preserve both the shared clip reference and each placement's transpose value.

origin.description: Illustrative request to reuse one clip at independent pitches.

canonicalMutations.rationale: This case distinguishes placement-specific playback and persistence from a copied or mutated clip.

payload.title: Play and reload two placements of one clip

steps.statement: One clip contains a C4 note. Two placements reference that clip; the first has transpose 0 and the second has transpose 2 semitones.
The user plays both placements, saves the arrangement, reloads it, and plays both placements again.
The first placement plays C4 and the second plays D4 before and after reload. Both placements still reference the one clip.
Playing or saving either placement rewrites the clip's C4 note or the other placement's transpose value.

origin.description: Illustrative acceptance case for placement-specific transposition and reload.

canonicalMutations.rationale: A placement refers to a reusable clip; the clip has no placement-owned position or transpose value.
The placement concept owns the transposition obligation.
The save and reload case demonstrates the transposition obligation.
